body:
**What was hard**
1. **Volume and noise.** Each call runs to about 9–11k words, and roughly 70% of that is restated strategy ("global delivery model", "best-cost country"). Only about 6–8 statements per call are real promises. Condensing to speaker turns (management in full, questions shortened) cut reading by about 40% without losing promises.
2. **Speaker attribution in pdftotext output is unreliable.** Labels such as "Q Management:", misspellings ("Parmjit", "Paramjit Sonis") and the CFO's turn sometimes tagged as a question all appear. A name list per company is needed, and the management list from the cover page should be parsed automatically.
3. **Deadlines are fuzzy.** "Second half next year" (calendar or fiscal? the speaker said calendar only when asked), "end of the year" (Dec-26 or Mar-27, resolved one call later), and "within the next year or so" all need a precision field plus a rule. Here: treat ambiguous as the later date, and record which one was assumed.
4. **Restatements versus new promises.** The same FY26 mid-teens guide was repeated in 5 calls. Counting each repeat inflates the "delivered" count. Logging only material restatements (after a shock or a change of speaker) fixed most of this, but a `restates: <id>` link is needed, with credit for the first statement only.
5. **Segment KPIs often can't be checked from outside.** Aftermarket, small ag, Mexico revenue and fabrication are reported only as percentages, now and then, and only when asked. The aftermarket miss had to be pieced together from share-of-revenue numbers in different calls. One promise (small-ag mid-teens) had to be marked "silently-dropped" because no number ever came back. That is the most debatable call in the set, so MCS is shown with and without it.
6. **Judging moved-goalpost against missed is subjective.** The line drawn here: a target revised before its deadline *without being called a revision* is moved-goalpost; a target missed after an honest restatement is missed. This rule should be written down and a second reviewer should check it.
7. **Era is confounded with the cycle.** A cyclical company guiding in a downturn will always score worse. MCS should be reported next to an industry cycle indicator, such as the change in Deere or CAT segment sales, or we will reward luck.
8. **Company-defined metrics.** Reported "EBITDA" includes other income, while screener OPM does not. Store both and score on the company's own definition (FY25: 17.3% against an 18% guide gives "partly"). Flag the gap.
title: UNIPARTS › 7. Lessons learned on the method

body:
`insight:buffett-retained-dollar-test` | confidence: verified | date: 1980-03-03

1979 letter: 'The primary test of managerial economic performance is the achievement of a high earnings rate on equity capital employed (without undue leverage, accounting gimmickry, etc.) and not the achievement of consistent gains in earnings per share.' EPS rose ~20% in 1979 but Buffett called it 'an improper figure upon which to focus' because EPS 'will rise constantly on a dormant savings account' when earnings are retained; 'even a stopped clock can look like a growth stock if the dividend payout ratio is low.' 1983 owner's manual: 'We test the wisdom of retaining earnings by assessing whether retention, over time, delivers shareholders at least $1 of market value for each $1 retained', on a five-year rolling basis; and 'We will issue common stock only when we receive as much in business value as we give.' 1984: unrestricted earnings should be retained only if reinvestment returns are at least what shareholders could earn themselves. Reaffirmed by Greg Abel in the 2025 letter: no dividends 'so long as more than one dollar of market value for shareholders is reasonably likely to be created by each dollar of retained earnings.' Actionable: compute for any Indian company over 5-10 yrs: (change in market cap) / (cumulative retained earnings). Below 1.0 = capital destruction regardless of EPS growth. Watch EPS growth that only reflects rising equity base at flat or falling ROE.

Sources:
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1979.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1983.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1984.html
- https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/2025ltr.pdf

body:
- 6 Motley Fool transcripts Q2-2025..Q3-2026 (the Q2-2026 call is listed twice; the 30-Jul-2026 copy is used). The CFO's outlook section was read in full on every call. CFO changed in Q3-2026 (Charles Lauber -> Carrie Anderson).
- Ledger built by hand (fetch.py reads NSE, not US sources): Motley Fool takeaway list + targeted greps of the full text (guidance, outlook, organic, adjusted operating margin, EPS, free cash flow / conversion, capex, savings, price/cost). Quotes marked [Fool summary] are the transcriber's takeaway wording, not management's words. Pipeline v1.3 adds the US measure vocabulary to `score.py` for future runs.
- Restatements are folded into the first promise (`later_restatements`), not double-counted; a cut >= 2 quarters before the deadline is 'withdrawn' (clarification A).
- Outcomes: company-adjusted KPIs (organic growth, adjusted operating margin, adjusted EPS, segment margins) from the company's own later calls/releases (single-source); GAAP revenue, operating income, EPS, capex, FCF, buybacks and dividends re-derived from SEC XBRL companyfacts (`tools/sec_fetch.py facts`) as the second source.
- Scoring: pilot formula unchanged (`scripts_TD_peers/build_seed.py`; T&D clarifications A-D apply). Credit delivered 1 / partly 0.5; MCS weights specificity x materiality x recency.

**Caveat: n is small** (6 calls; 6-18 scored promises; most FY2026 guidance pending). Categories rarely reach the L18 threshold of 5 scored promises with 2+ peers, so SAC is computed on pooled categories and shrunk toward zero (N/(N+20)) when used.
